meta.about: Script for the Face Feelings demo. See GAME_DESIGN.md section 'story.json format' for every field.

placeholders.{name}: Character name chosen by the child: Miso or Sam.
placeholders.{friend}: The other character, who is {name}'s friend in the story: Sam when the child picked Miso, Miso when the child picked Sam. From characters[].friendId.
placeholders.{hand}: Per-character word from characters[].words.hand (hand or paw).
placeholders.{word}: Lower-case emotion word from emotions[id].word, e.g. 'sad'.
placeholders.{sticker}: Sticker label of the current scene, e.g. 'a red balloon'.

textRules: Each string is one sentence or one short spoken unit. The app shows it and, if read-aloud is on, speaks it.
Scene text never names the emotion, so difficulty level 3 (neutral face) works.
No all-caps words: some speech engines spell them out letter by letter.

happy.label: Happy
hint: The mouth corners go up, in a big smile.

coach.text: Push the corners of your mouth up.
Smile bigger, so your cheeks go up.

sad.label: Sad
hint: The eyebrows go up in the middle.

coach.text: Lift the middle of your eyebrows.
Pull the corners of your mouth down.

surprised.label: Surprised
hint: The eyebrows go up high, and the eyes open wide.

angry.label: Angry
hint: The eyebrows go down and close together.

coach.text: Pull your eyebrows down and together.

scared.label: Scared
hint: The eyebrows go up, and the eyes open wide.
The mouth stretches out to the sides.

coach.text: Stretch your mouth out to the sides.

home.privacyShort: Everything stays on this phone. No accounts. No recording. Nothing is uploaded.

characterPick.prompt: Who do you want to play with today?

askPermission: To play, the game uses the front camera.
Grown-ups: please tap Allow when the phone asks.
The camera picture stays on this phone.
denied: That's OK. You can still play.
You can tap the faces, and the story goes on.
faceLost: Let's find your face. Look at the phone.
Where is your face? Look at the screen.
camera.tooDark: A little more light will help.
camera.tooFar: Come a little closer to the phone.

calibration.retry: Let's try that again. Keep your face still.

intro: Find out how {name} feels. Then make the same face!
outro: Now the sun goes down. It is time for bed.

lookCloser.point: Look at the eyebrows. Look at the mouth.

niceTry: Nice try! Let's see what happens next.
Thank you for trying! On we go.

spoken: OK! Let's see what happens next.

noCamera.prompt: Make {name}'s {word} face. Tap Done when you are ready.

mirror.title: Mirror
mirror.intro: Make a face. {name} will copy you!
ideas: Try lifting your eyebrows up high.

adultGate.label: Grown-ups: press and hold for 3 seconds.

privacyNote: Face Feelings uses the front camera to follow the shape of the face: eyebrows, eyes, nose and mouth.
The camera picture is checked on this phone and then thrown away. Nothing is recorded, saved or sent anywhere.
There are no accounts. The game saves only your settings, the calm-face measurement and the sticker book, and only on this phone.
The game measures face movements only. It does not decide how anyone feels.
Tap 'Clear saved data' to delete everything the game has saved.

settings.label: Emotions
settings.help: Choose which faces appear. For a child who is new to this, start with Happy and Sad, then add Surprised and Angry, then Scared and Disgusted.

settings.label: Number of cards
settings.help: How many faces the child chooses from. Fewer cards is easier. Cannot be more than the number of emotions that are on.

settings.label: Sensitivity
settings.help: How big a face movement fills the meter. High: a small movement is enough (easier). Low: the face must be bigger and clearer.

settings.label: Hold time
settings.help: How long the face must stay full on the meter before it counts.

settings.label: Time limit
settings.help: How long the child has to make the face. When time ends, the game says 'Nice try!' and moves on. Off: the game waits until the face is made or Skip is tapped.

settings.label: Face style
settings.help: How strongly the character shows each feeling. Big is easiest to read. Difficulty level 4 always uses Subtle.

settings.label: Difficulty level
settings.help: 1: copy the character's face, no story. 2: story, and the character shows the feeling. 3: story, the character's face stays calm, so the child works it out from what happens. 4: like 3, with subtle faces on the cards.

settings.label: Read aloud
settings.help: The phone's voice reads the story and the instructions.

settings.label: Camera preview
settings.help: Shows the child's camera picture in a small window. Some children find it helpful. Others find it distracting.

settings.label: Session length
settings.help: How many scenes in one story. The happy party scene is always last.

settings.label: Show detection details
settings.help: For grown-ups: shows bars with what the camera measures. Useful for testing. Turn it off for children.

settings.label: Recalibrate
settings.help: Measure the calm face again. Do this when the light changes or a different person plays.

settings.label: Sound effects
settings.help: Story sounds like the dog barking or thunder. Soft keeps them quiet, for children who are sensitive to sudden sounds.

settings.label: Clear saved data
settings.help: Deletes settings, the calm-face measurement and the sticker book from this phone.

text: {name} wakes up and looks out of the window.
It is summer, but it is snowing!
comfort: The sun comes out, and the snow melts away.
Time for breakfast!
scenes.illustration: Bedroom with a bed and one big window. Outside: a green summer tree with snowflakes falling on it. A sun hat on a chair shows that it is summer.
scenes.comfortIllustration: Same window, sun shining, snow almost gone.

text: {name} pours a glass of milk and smells it.
The milk is old. It smells very bad!
comfort: {friend} pours the old milk away.
{friend} gives {name} fresh orange juice instead. It smells nice and sweet.
scenes.illustration: Kitchen table with a bowl, a milk carton and a glass of milk. Two small wavy green smell lines rise from the glass. Simple cupboard and window behind.
scenes.comfortIllustration: Same table, a glass of orange juice in place of the milk.

text: At the park, {name} gets a big red balloon on a string.
Red is {name}'s favorite color!
scenes.illustration: Park with grass, one tree, a bench and a path. A balloon stand on the side. The red balloon is the only strong color in the picture.

text: Whoosh! The wind pulls the balloon string away from {name}.
The red balloon floats up, up, up into the sky.
comfort: {friend} has two balloons.
{friend} gives one to {name}. Now they each have a balloon.
scenes.illustration: Same park as the red balloon scene. The red balloon is high in the sky, small. A few leaves blow to show the wind.
scenes.comfortIllustration: The friend character (Sam or Miso, whichever the child did not pick; calm, kind face) holds out a yellow balloon to the character.

text: {name} builds a tower with blocks. One block, two blocks, ten blocks!
It is the tallest tower {name} has ever made.
scenes.illustration: Playroom with a soft rug, a toy shelf and a window. A tall tower of colored blocks, taller than the character.

text: {name} has a very tall tower of blocks.
{friend} pushes the tower over, on purpose.
Crash! All the blocks fall down.
comfort: {friend} comes back and says, 'I am sorry. That was not kind.'
Then the two of them build the tower again, together.
scenes.illustration: Same playroom. Blocks scattered on the rug. The friend character is seen from behind or the side, walking away; no mean face.
scenes.comfortIllustration: Miso and Sam placing blocks on a new tower side by side, calm faces.

text: In the park, a big dog runs up to {name}.
Woof! Woof! The dog barks very loudly.
comfort: {friend} calls, 'Rufus, come here!'
The dog sits down next to {friend} and wags its tail. Rufus is {friend}'s dog, and he is friendly.
scenes.illustration: Same park, path in front. A big brown dog with an open mouth mid-bark, front paws on the ground (not jumping on the character). The friend character far back with a leash, running to catch up.
scenes.comfortIllustration: Dog sitting next to the friend character, tail up, mouth closed or tongue out.

text: {name} finds a toy box with a little handle and turns it round and round.
Music plays. Then, pop! A toy jumps out of the box on a spring!
comfort: It is a jack-in-the-box.
{name} pushes the toy back in, ready to play again.
scenes.illustration: Living room with a sofa, a lamp and a rug. A bright box with a crank handle; a soft puppet on a spring has popped out. Use a smiling sun or bird puppet, not a clown.
scenes.comfortIllustration: The box closed again, lid on top.

text: {name} has a picnic in the garden and takes a big bite of an apple.
Inside the apple there is a little wiggly worm!
comfort: {name} puts the apple on the grass for the worm.
{friend} gives {name} a banana instead. It is clean and sweet.
scenes.illustration: Garden with grass, a picnic blanket, a fence and a flower bed. A green apple with a bite out of it and a small pink cartoon worm peeking out.
scenes.comfortIllustration: Apple on the grass with the worm; a yellow banana on the blanket.

text: At the bakery, {name} carries a chocolate cake to the table.
The cake slips. Splat! It falls on the floor.
comfort: {friend} comes over with a smile.
{friend} shares a cupcake with a cherry on top. 'Accidents happen,' says {friend}.
scenes.illustration: Bakery with a glass counter, a few cakes on shelves and a small round table. A chocolate cake upside down on the floor; no mess beyond one brown splat.
scenes.comfortIllustration: The friend character (calm, kind face) holding out a cupcake with a cherry.

text: In the afternoon, the sky goes dark.
There is a flash of lightning. Then, boom! The thunder is very loud.
comfort: {friend} sits next to {name} and holds {name}'s {hand}.
The two of them wait together until the storm is over. Then the sun comes out again.
scenes.illustration: Same living room as the jack-in-the-box scene. Big window with a grey sky, rain and one lightning bolt. Show lightning as a soft glow, never a flashing screen.
scenes.comfortIllustration: Same window, rainbow and sun. Miso and Sam on the sofa together.

text: Today is party day!
Ding dong! {friend} is at the door, with cake and balloons!
scenes.illustration: Same garden as the picnic scene, now with bunting, a table with a cake and balloons. The friend character (Sam or Miso, whichever the child did not pick) at the door, both characters waving with happy faces.

text: {name} helps make pancakes. Mix, pour, flip!
The pancakes are round and warm, and {name} gets the first one.
extraScenes.illustration: Same kitchen as the milk scene. A plate with a stack of pancakes and a jug of syrup.

text: At the bakery, {name} and {friend} put sprinkles on a big cake.
Lots and lots of sprinkles!
extraScenes.illustration: Same bakery. A white cake on the counter covered in colored sprinkles, a sprinkle shaker next to it.

text: {name}'s favorite toy car has a broken wheel.
The car cannot roll any more.
comfort: {friend} helps fix the wheel with glue.
Tomorrow the car can roll again.
extraScenes.illustration: Same bedroom. A small blue toy car on the floor, one wheel lying next to it.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: The friend character gluing the wheel back on; a glue tube on the floor.

text: {name} builds a sandcastle on the beach.
A wave comes and washes the sandcastle away.
comfort: {name} builds a new sandcastle, higher up on the sand.
The waves cannot reach it there.
extraScenes.illustration: Beach with calm blue sea, sand and a bucket and spade. A flat wet patch where the sandcastle was, a small wave going back.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: A new sandcastle with a little flag, far from the water.

text: {name} watches corn seeds in a pot with a glass lid.
Then, pop, pop, pop! The seeds jump up and turn into popcorn!
comfort: Now there is a big bowl of warm popcorn.
extraScenes.illustration: Same kitchen. A pot with a glass lid on the stove, white popcorn bouncing inside.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: A bowl of popcorn on the table.

text: {name} lifts up a big leaf in the garden.
Hop! A little rabbit jumps out from under it!
comfort: The rabbit hops away into the bushes.
extraScenes.illustration: Same garden. A large leafy plant, a small grey rabbit mid-hop.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: Rabbit tail disappearing into a bush.

text: {name} wants to go outside, but the zip on the coat is stuck.
{name} pulls and pulls. The zip stays stuck, again and again.
comfort: {friend} shows how to do it: hold the bottom, then pull slowly.
Zip! The coat is closed. Off to the park!
extraScenes.illustration: Hallway with a front door, a coat hook and a shoe rack. The character wears an open coat; the zip is shown clearly.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: Coat zipped up, front door open to sunshine.

text: {name} is drawing a big picture of a house.
{friend} says, 'Stop now. It is time to go to the bakery.' The picture is not finished.
comfort: 'You can finish it when we come home,' says {friend}.
{name} puts the picture in a safe place on the shelf.
extraScenes.illustration: Same playroom. A small table with crayons and a half-colored drawing of a house.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: The drawing lying flat on a shelf.

text: {name} goes into the garden shed. It is dark inside.
Something moves in the corner. Rustle, rustle!
comfort: {friend} opens the door wide, and the light comes in.
It is a little bird. The bird flies out into the garden.
extraScenes.illustration: Inside a wooden shed, dim but not black: a watering can, a rake on the wall. A small dark shape in the corner. Keep it dim, never scary detail.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: Shed door open, sunlight, a small brown bird flying out.

text: {name} is playing on the beach.
A big wave rushes up the sand, very fast, right up to {name}!
comfort: {friend} takes {name}'s {hand}, and they run up the sand together.
The wave slides back into the sea. Now the two of them play on the dry sand.
extraScenes.illustration: Same beach. A big white-topped wave reaching up the sand towards the character. No deep water, no one in the water.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: Miso and Sam hand in hand on dry sand, wave going back, calm sea.

text: At the bakery, {name} picks up an old bread roll from the back of a shelf.
Underneath, the bread is green and fuzzy. It is moldy!
comfort: {friend} puts the old roll in the bin.
Then {friend} gives {name} a fresh, warm roll.
extraScenes.illustration: Same bakery. A bread roll turned over, with soft green fuzzy spots underneath.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: A golden fresh roll in a paper bag.

text: {name} steps on a pile of seaweed.
It is cold and slimy, and it smells like old fish.
comfort: {name} washes the slime off in the clean sea water.
All clean again!
extraScenes.illustration: Same beach. A pile of dark green seaweed on the sand, two small smell lines above it.
extraScenes.comfortIllustration: Character at the edge of small calm waves, splashing water.
